generators.name: stochastic mutation generator
generators.description: Propose codon-synonymous DNA candidates via random mutations during local region optimization.

evidence.quote: A region's sequence is optimized via either a stochastic search (using random mutations of the sequence) or an exhaustive search through all possible sequence variants, depending on the number of variants.

constraints.name: windowed GC content
constraints.description: Keep GC content between 40 and 60 percent on every 100-nucleotide window across the NUM1 coding sequence.

evidence.quote: Gene NUM1 of Saccharomyces cerevisiae will be codon optimized for Escherischia coli, and have a GC content of 40-60% on every 100-nucleotide window.

constraints.name: BsaI site removal
constraints.description: Remove BsaI restriction sites (GGTCTC) that impede DNA synthesis and assembly.

evidence.quote: BsaI restriction sites will be removed (@no(BsaI_site) constraint).

constraints.name: homopolymer limit
constraints.description: Reject homopolymer runs that impede synthesis.

evidence.quote: Removal of regulatory elements or elements impeding DNA synthesis and assembly.

constraints.name: k-mer uniqueness
constraints.description: Remove undesirable homologies using codon-synonymous mutations in the coding region.

evidence.quote: Undesirable homologies occurring naturally in the gene sequence will be removed in the region marked @all_unique_kmers, using codon-synonymous mutations only, as enforced by the @cds constraint.

constraints.name: codon optimization
constraints.description: Optimize codon usage for Escherichia coli expression while preserving the amino acid sequence.

evidence.quote: Gene NUM1 of Saccharomyces cerevisiae will be codon optimized for Escherischia coli

optimizers.name: region-local MCMC refinement
optimizers.description: Detect unsatisfactory regions and run stochastic local search per region until constraints converge.

evidence.quote: During each step, unsatisfactory sequence regions are detected and separately optimized.
The optimization algorithm ... has two main steps: (1) resolution of all hard constraints, ignoring optimization objectives, and (2) objectives maximization with respect to the constraints.

model_dependencies.name: Biopython
model_dependencies.purpose: Genbank operations and restriction enzyme data in DNA Chisel

evidence.quote: DNA Chisel is implemented in Python. It relies on the Biopython library (Cock et al., 2009) for Genbank operations and restriction enzyme data.

steps.operation: resolve hard constraints on unsatisfactory regions

evidence.quote: During each step, unsatisfactory sequence regions are detected and separately optimized.

steps.operation: score windowed GC, pattern, k-mer, and codon constraints
maximize weighted objectives under satisfied constraints

evidence.quote: This steps separation allows to detect incompatible constraints early, and quickly reach satisfactory solutions.

assumptions: NUM1 CDS length set to 936 bp (Saccharomyces cerevisiae coding sequence scale).
Region-local solver runs all outer passes plus inner window refinements per DNA Chisel's per-region stochastic search.
Codon optimization uses a static E. coli codon usage table rather than the Codon Usage Database API.
K-mer uniqueness approximates @all_unique_kmers via overrepresentation penalties on 6-mers.
unknowns: Protected promoter/terminer flanks (@keep annotations) are not modeled in v1.
Exact DNA Chisel exhaustive vs stochastic region solver switching is not reproduced.
AvoidMatches homology removal against external reference genomes is not bound in v1.
